title: Spectrahedrality of Hyperbolicity Cones
exact_target: Let $h$ be a real homogeneous polynomial hyperbolic in a direction $e$, meaning that $h(e)>0$ and $t\mapsto h(x-te)$ has only real zeros for every real vector $x$. Must its closed hyperbolicity cone be expressible as $\{x:\sum_i x_iA_i\succeq0\}$ for real symmetric matrices $A_i$? Such a cone is spectrahedral.
